A worker tried to cancel a finished ticket and sent a note to a finished agent; both failed silently in effect, and the ticket dispatch skill says nothing about either limit.
Recall gap: this episode used the skill for releasing, cancelling and writing tickets, and the description only named dispatch and ordering.

Two parallel tickets (ref records and module deletion) both touched the store layout and map module; the coordinating note had to settle who goes first, and the timing of delivery was observed.
Two concrete dispatch_note failures in this episode (reply to a finished agent, 1004-char note) are not documented; the existing bullet covers only the outbound case.

In the episode, a spec workflow finished mid-flight. The system agent cited CTX records onto eight tickets and sent dispatch messages to the two running agents, which is a repeatable step the skill does not describe.

Worker closed ticket code.graph.knowledge#12 with op=done and said=; the tool replied that said was ignored, so the closing text had to go in resolution. The rule is a tool pitfall that future workers will hit on every ticket close.
The moving-link rule as written reads as covering any link, which is how a ref ticket inherited a rule that only applies to properties. Reconciles it with the ref ruling.
Two dispatch_note calls failed on selector misuse, and a peer reported hitting the hourly note limit; the wait timeout was misread as a failure. These are not in the skill yet.

After #17 landed, the agent had to warn running tickets that the MCP server and runners still ran the old refs code. That warning should be the standard step on landing a change that others depend on.

Two dispatch pitfalls seen in this episode that no existing ticket-dispatch bullet covers: completions sweep unrelated uncommitted work into one commit, and a message to an idle agent is silently not acted on.

The line said completions commit the shared tree and gave no guard. The episode found the bug in checkpoint() and finished(), added a worktree-only guard and a test. The dispatch skill should say so, so the next agent checks the guard before relying on it.

The episode chose dispatch new over a page-side stop-then-start because stop switches Stay connected off and a stopped worker keeps its ticket, so start refuses. Future dispatch work needs that pitfall in the ticket-dispatch skill.
